mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in CPIAUCSL above 3% over three consecutive months signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or CPI remains below 3% during the period following the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers above 2% within the 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in UNRATE for three consecutive months indicates a tightening labor market, which raises wage pressures and leads to higher corporate costs and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as inflation fears rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by > 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or UNRATE falls below the pre-trigger level within 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in INDPRO signals a contraction in industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or INDPRO rebounds by more than 1% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 2% in both GDPC1 and HOUST signals a broad-based weakening in housing and overall demand, which depresses consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -2.0% AND HOUST monthly change < -2.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of co-triggered episodes, or either GDPC1 or HOUST rebounds above the trigger threshold within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 5% while CPIAUCSL is above 4% for three consecutive months, the combination signals aggressive monetary tightening in response to high inflation, which increases discount rates and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5.0% AND CPIAUCSL > 4.0% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of co-triggered episodes, or FEDFUNDS falls below 5% before the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in PAYEMS of more than 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or PAYEMS growth slows to below 0.2% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between RSAFS growth above 1% month-over-month and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as rising household savings typically precede increased consumer spending and stronger corporate performance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in more than 70% of triggered months, or RSAFS growth above 1% is followed by a decline in RSAFS in the subsequent month.
